snippet: In its preliminary IPO registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Anthropic describes how much of its capacity depends on a small group of chip and memory suppliers, most of them in East Asia.

title: Tamil Nadu adds independent chip subsidy route as Indian states vie for investment
snippet: India's semiconductor drive has largely been led by New Delhi, which selects projects for large central incentives while state governments add their own packages of land, infrastructure and financial support. Tamil Nadu is now giving semiconductor investors another route.

title: OPTOELEC seeks AI data center orders as Himax advances CPO optics
snippet: South Korean optics maker Optoelec is seeing growing interest from AI data center customers as it seeks to expand its wafer-level optics (WLO) business into high-speed optical communications, a market where Taiwanese suppliers are already moving toward commercial production.

title: NT1 plans to assemble Chinese delivery vans in Korea in 2027
snippet: South Korean autonomous delivery company NT1 plans to begin assembling Chinese-designed delivery vans locally in 2027, gradually adding Korean-made components as it seeks approval to operate the vehicles on public roads.

title: Hyundai supplier SL eyes first overseas robot deployment in US
snippet: South Korean automotive supplier SL is considering deploying its mobile dual-arm robot at a US factory in 2027 or 2028, potentially marking the system's first overseas deployment, a company representative said in an interview with DIGITIMES at FIX 2026 in Daegu on October 24.

title: Tata Communications plans up to US$450 million fibre network linking India's AI hubs
snippet: Tata Communications announced on October 26 that it plans to invest US$400-450 million in approximately 10,000 kilometers of long-haul fiber across India, linking data centers and AI hubs as it expands its connectivity business. The network will connect domestic corridors with its global backbone.

title: KAR bets on fleet monitoring as South Korea expands robotaxi trials
snippet: South Korean vehicle engineering company KAR plans to develop a monitoring system for the electronic controls it installs in autonomous vehicles, seeking recurring maintenance revenue as the country expands robotaxi trials.

title: ByteDance denies AI micro-dramas consume over half of China's AI computing power
snippet: The claim that more than half of China's artificial intelligence (AI) computing power is being used to produce micro-dramas has reignited debate in China's technology sector over whether the country is directing too much of its AI computing resources to entertainment content while neglecting productivity applications.

title: Amkor turns to customer prepayments as global packaging investment accelerates
snippet: Amkor Technology is using customer prepayments and longer-term commitments to support an expanding manufacturing network across the US, South Korea, and Vietnam, as demand for advanced packaging outpaces the consumer electronics recovery. Management said those arrangements provide greater visibility for investments that will keep capital spending elevated for several years.

title: Cadence bets on its own chip design AI models as Synopsys teams up with OpenAI
snippet: Cadence Design Systems is betting that chipmakers will want AI models trained on its own design tools and run wherever customers choose. That puts it on a different route from rival Synopsys, which is building its specialized model with OpenAI on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure. On October 26, alongside its third-quarter results, Cadence introduced Maestro, a portfolio of domain-specialized AI models that power its AI super agents for chip and system design.

title: Cadence says chip design demand is broadening beyond AI as analysts test margins, rival targets
snippet: Cadence Design Systems used its third-quarter earnings call to argue that demand for chip design tools is no longer tied only to the AI hardware buildout. It pointed to analog and memory chipmakers, system companies, and new entrants such as space and finance firms designing their own silicon. title: BlackRock’s Rieder Spent All Weekend Doing Deals in AI Debt Rush
snippet: The AI-driven debt boom is creating some of the most attractive fixed-income opportunities in years, eclipsing the appeal of long-dated US Treasuries, according to BlackRock’s Rick Rieder.
